findings.claim: No test in this diff ever drives `_batch_runner`'s adapter through a `READY_FOR_REVIEW` outcome, so the packaging branch at lines 586-600 — including the `outcome.state = result.state` overwrite the docstring calls out as necessary ('reflects what actually happened to the task — MERGE_FAILED included') — is never exercised. Both new adapter witnesses (`test_the_adapter_stacks_a_child_on_its_parents_branch` and `test_the_adapter_stacks_on_the_first_dependency_only`) stub `run_one_cell` to raise `SystemExit` immediately, short-circuiting before this branch is reached. Deleting the line `outcome.state = result.state` leaves every test in the suite green.

The `.ok` check that distinguishes a readiness failure from an ordinary mid-loop breaker firing is only exercised at its two extremes: `test_infrastructure_and_a_failed_readiness_both_exit_two`'s breaker case fakes `run_batch` entirely (so `readiness_check` is never called and `readiness_seen` stays empty), and its readiness case makes `check_readiness` fail immediately. No witness runs the real `run_batch` with a readiness that succeeds and then lets the breaker fire from candidate aborts, which is the actual real-world 'breaker firing' case the acceptance criterion names. Widening the condition to `if readiness_seen:` (dropping `.ok`) would make a genuine mid-loop breaker print the nonsensical `batch: readiness failed at None: None` instead of `batch: infrastructure failed`, and every test in this diff would still pass.
